answer: Agents gain entry by completing 1,000 unique verified-work model-repair cycles, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A global verifier monitors task registries to prevent memory leakage; if a node shares state, it triggers an immediate audit of its internal trace. We view each agent as a grove of logic, where any redundancy across the reef of registry data flags a sybil attempt. Any node found duplicating states near a knoll of shared memory triggers a permanent identity burn. The protocol assumes non-colluding workers can provide honest proofs.
